units.title: Sound Lines: service update, day 8
units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines service update, 06:30. The fog warning remains in force until 10:00. Early crossings are operating under fog procedure at reduced speed. The 06:40 Gilliver departure is expected into Port Ammet about 20 minutes late. Freight will be carried on the 07:30 and later sailings. Thank you for your patience.

units.title: Marrow Sound forecast, day 8
units.author: met
units.text: Forecast for the Marrow Sound, day 8. Fog and low cloud slow to clear, with visibility mostly 200 to 800 metres, improving inland during the afternoon. A southwesterly breeze will reach the outer islands this evening and clear the fog from west to east overnight. Maximum 9 C. Outlook: day 9 bright and breezy, wind southwest 4 to 5, risk of a shower in the west.

units.title: Tides, day 8
units.author: met
units.text: Tide times, day 8. Port Ammet: high water 05:31 (4.3 m) and 17:58 (4.5 m); low water 11:46 (0.9 m), next low 00:12 on day 9. Gilliver about 12 minutes later; Lisle about 6 minutes earlier. Spring tides: expect strong streams in the Holm channel and off Carrow Point.

units.title: Notice to mariners: survey launch, Port Ammet approaches
units.author: coast
units.text: Notice to mariners. A survey launch will work in the Port Ammet approaches between 08:00 and 16:00 on day 8 and day 9, showing the appropriate day shapes. Give it a wide berth and pass at slow speed. The Lisle South cardinal buoy remains unlit; a repair visit is planned for day 9.

units.title: Recycling collections: update
units.author: council
units.text: Waste collection update. Recycling in Rope Walk, Chandler Street and Mill Lane will be collected today. Residents whose containers were not emptied yesterday should leave them out. Collections in these streets return to the normal day next week. Thank you for your patience.

units.title: Planning information: please use the register
units.author: council
units.text: Planning information. The council's online planning register is the only authoritative record of applications, descriptions and decisions in Ammet District. Copies, screenshots or summaries found elsewhere may be incomplete or altered. To check an application, search the register by reference or address. Officers cannot comment on material that does not come from the register.

units.title: Fog warning expired
units.author: met
units.text: The yellow warning for fog expired at 10:00. Patchy fog will persist on coasts and islands through the day, dense in places, especially around Gilliver and Kittering Holm. Visibility will improve steadily from the west this evening as the breeze arrives.

units.title: Unplanned interruption: Port Ammet harbour area
units.author: power
units.text: Supply was interrupted to 212 properties in the Port Ammet harbour area from 11:04 to 11:22 after a vehicle struck a pole on Quay Road in poor visibility. Supply has been restored. Engineers will replace the damaged pole later this week, and customers will be given notice of any planned interruption.

units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines update, 12:30. Freight will be carried on tonight's 19:30 Port Ammet sailing. Afternoon crossings are running to time. We expect a full normal timetable from the first sailing on day 9. Thank you for your patience this week. The terminal cafe's soup offer ends today, sadly.

units.title: Advance notice: Gilliver Back Road
units.author: power
units.text: Advance notice. Sound Power Co-op will replace a pole-mounted transformer on Gilliver Back Road on day 10 between 09:30 and 14:00. Around 60 properties, including the chandlery and the harbour office, will be without supply. Cards are being delivered. The harbour navigation lights are on a separate supply and are not affected.

units.title: Small craft advice to lift from day 9
units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard advice. With visibility forecast to improve overnight, the advice for small craft to remain ashore will be lifted from 06:00 on day 9, subject to conditions. Expect a lumpy sea where spring tides run against the southwesterly. Check the forecast, wear a lifejacket and tell someone where you are going.

units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines update, 20:00. All evening crossings are running to time. The last night crossing from Port Ammet will run as scheduled. Lookouts remain posted at night as normal. Passengers are reminded not to use the vehicle deck stairs while the vessel is berthing.

units.title: Evening update, day 8
units.author: met
units.text: Evening update. The southwesterly breeze has reached Lisle and the outer Sound, and the fog is breaking up from the west. Gilliver and Kittering Holm should clear by around midnight. Tomorrow: bright, breezy and cooler, wind southwest 4 to 5, a shower or two in the west. Tides remain large.

units.title: Live: the last day of the fog
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 06:35. Morning. The fog warning runs until 10:00 and it is still thick at the coast, about 100 metres at Gilliver and a little better in Port Ammet. The good news, according to the Met Office: this should be the last foggy morning of the week.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 07:20. Ferries running at reduced speed, the 06:40 from Gilliver about 20 minutes behind. Freight is back on from the 07:30. Several listeners report the Lisle South buoy is still dark, which the Coastguard already knows about and would like you to stop ringing them about.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 09:10. A reminder after a near miss on the Tollinby road: if you break down in fog, get out of the car and well away from the carriageway, then call for help. Don't sit in it with the hazards on. The road past the reservoir has had two minor bumps already this morning.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 11:30. A power cut in the Port Ammet harbour area lasted about twenty minutes after a lorry hit a pole on Quay Road. Supply is back. The driver is fine. The pole is not, and will be replaced later in the week.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 14:40. It is brightening in Tollinby and Brackwater, with actual patches of blue. The coast is still holding on to the grey. Sound Lines say freight will run on tonight's 19:30 and a full normal timetable is expected from first thing tomorrow.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 18:10. Final fog update of the week, we hope. The breeze has reached Lisle and visibility there is up to two kilometres. Gilliver should follow by midnight. Thank you for your reports all week. We will keep the soup jokes to ourselves from now on, mostly.

units.title: Overnight show: your fog stories
units.author: soundfm
units.text: Listeners to the overnight show spent much of last night trading fog stories. A caller from Lisle walked into her own hedge and apologised to it. A Tollinby man went twice round the same roundabout before realising it was the same roundabout. A Gilliver caller said he had found his way home by the smell of the chip shop.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: The show's producer said fog brings out the best in callers. 'People ring because they can't see anything and want to hear somebody,' she said. 'Then they tell you about the hedge.' The overnight show returns at midnight, with fewer hedges expected.

units.title: Council warns over altered Holm planning image
units.author: courier
units.text: An image shared online that claims to show the planning notice for Kittering Holm has been altered, Ammet District Council said today. The image adds the words 'to facilitate a designated evacuation site' to the description of a vegetation clearance consent. The council's register contains no such wording.

units.author: courier
units.text: A planning consultant who compared the image with the register entry said the added line used a different typeface and spacing from the rest of the notice, and that the reference number shown belongs to a different application altogether, a garage extension in Tollinby. 'Someone has pasted a sentence into a picture,' she said.

units.author: courier
units.text: The image was posted on a local forum by a man who runs a mailing list about local affairs. He said he had received it from a subscriber and had never claimed it was genuine. 'I asked a question,' he said. The forum's administrator removed the image this morning.

units.author: courier
units.text: Ardent Vale Holdings, which owns the island, said it did not comment on speculation. A council spokesperson said the consent covered vegetation clearance only, and that any further development would need a separate application and a public consultation.

units.title: Breeze to end fog week, forecasters say
units.author: courier
units.text: Forecasters expect a southwesterly breeze to clear the fog from the Marrow Sound tonight, ending five days of grey that have delayed ferries, kept fishing boats in harbour and cancelled two school swimming trips.

units.author: courier
units.text: The Met Office said the fog had been a classic case of mild, moist air moving over cold water. 'It needed wind, and there wasn't any,' a forecaster said. Tomorrow is expected to be bright and breezy, with spring tides and a lively sea in the channels.

units.title: Lorry hits pole on Quay Road in fog
units.author: courier
units.text: A delivery lorry struck a power pole on Quay Road, Port Ammet, this morning, cutting electricity to around 200 properties in the harbour area for twenty minutes. Nobody was hurt.

units.author: courier
units.text: The driver told a passer-by he had not seen the pole until his wing mirror met it. Sound Power Co-op said the pole would be replaced later this week. The Harbour Cafe, which lost power in the lunchtime rush, said it had 'served cold soup with confidence'.

units.title: Port Ammet library to open late three evenings a week
units.author: courier
units.text: Port Ammet library will stay open until 20:00 three evenings a week from next month, after a survey found that most residents in work could not visit before the current closing time of 17:00.

units.author: courier
units.text: The library said the late openings would be covered by existing staff on later shifts rather than new hires. Entries to the council's photo competition, on the theme of the Sound at work, will hang in the reading room from the first late evening.

units.title: Gilliver lifeboat open day moved
units.author: courier
units.text: The Gilliver lifeboat station's open day, planned for this week, has been put back by a fortnight because the fog stopped volunteers from finishing the repainting of the boathouse doors.

units.author: courier
units.text: The crew said the new date would also give time for the station's new floodlights to be fitted. Visitors will be able to see the boat, try on the kit and watch a demonstration of a casualty being brought up the slipway on a stretcher.

units.title: Council to review tower block lift contracts
units.author: weypost
units.text: Weyhaven City Council is to review maintenance arrangements for lifts in privately managed tower blocks after complaints from residents in four buildings, including Dellow Court, where tenants say the lift has been out of service on three of the past eight days.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The council has limited powers over private managers, but a housing officer said repeated lift failures could be treated as disrepair where elderly or disabled residents were affected. 'We are not able to fix a lift,' she said. 'We are able to ask why it keeps breaking, in writing.'

units.author: weypost
units.text: Kerrow Estates, which manages Dellow Court, said its lift engineer was booked for tomorrow and that it took the safety of residents seriously. Residents are meeting tonight to discuss the lift and a lighting fault in the block's stairwell.

units.title: Weyhaven port adds night shifts to clear fog backlog
units.author: weypost
units.text: Weyhaven's container port has added extra night shifts to clear a backlog of ships delayed by the fog in the Sound. Eleven vessels were waiting at anchor this morning, the most since last winter's storms.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Dockers' representatives said the overtime was welcome but asked for better lighting in the outer yards, where several floodlights have failed. The port said a lighting contractor would begin work next week.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Hauliers expect delays at the port gate to continue as containers move inland. The port has advised drivers to book collection slots online rather than queue on the dock road, where tailbacks reached the second roundabout this afternoon.

units.title: Grieve's Holm contract: the rates in context
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: The Kittering Holm clearance, carried out by Grieve Land Services for Ardent Vale Holdings, pays $100 per tree plus $300 per worker per day, according to people familiar with the terms. Both figures are above the regional average, the per-tree price markedly so.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Contractors who looked at the figures for this journal said the premium reflects the logistics: an island with no road, a crew living on site, timber that must leave by boat and a thirty-day deadline. 'It's good money if nothing goes wrong,' one said. 'On an island, everything goes wrong slowly.'

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Grieve has a long record of large clearances, including several on remote sites in the north. The company did not respond to questions about the Holm, and Ardent Vale has said little beyond confirming that it owns the island and is in no hurry.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Total vegetation clearance at this scale is unusual in the Sound, where most consents are for selective felling or thinning. Planning consultants point out that clearance consent does not by itself permit any building, road or other development on the land.

units.title: Chainsaw ticket refresher backlog grows
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Training providers in the Sound report waiting lists of up to eight weeks for chainsaw ticket refresher courses, after a run of site inspections reminded contractors that lapsed tickets void insurance cover on many jobs.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: One assessor called the backlog entirely predictable. 'Everybody's ticket was issued in the same year after the last big storm, so now they all fall due at once.' Several self-employed operators said they had turned down work while they waited for a course date.

units.title: Ammet District Council: your weekly update
units.author: council_news
units.text: Bins: recycling rounds in Rope Walk, Chandler Street and Mill Lane were delayed this week after a collection vehicle was damaged in the fog. Missed containers are being collected today. Thank you to everyone who left their boxes out, and to the resident who rang us eleven times to make sure we knew.

units.author: council_news
units.text: Roads: the temporary lights at the Brackwater junction will stay in place until day 14 while the culvert works are finished. The lights run a fixed cycle for the safety of the work crew. Please be patient, and please don't wave other drivers through on red, however kind it feels.

units.author: council_news
units.text: Have your say: we are consulting on new parking arrangements for the Port Ammet harbour car park, including resident permits and a two-hour limit for visitors. The consultation closes at the end of the month. Paper copies are available at the library and the harbour office.

units.author: council_news
units.text: Photo competition: there is still time to enter 'The Sound at Work'. We have had some lovely entries so far, including a ferry in fog, a net loft in Gilliver and a very good dog supervising a bin lorry. Entries close at the end of the month.

units.author: council_news
units.text: Libraries: Port Ammet library will open until 20:00 three evenings a week from next month. Tollinby's mobile library van is back on the road after repairs and will visit Brackwater and the reservoir cottages on its usual route, with a new large-print shelf.

units.author: council_news
units.text: Planning: applications determined this week include a garage extension in Tollinby, two householder applications on Lisle and a change of use for the old net loft on Gilliver quay. As always, the online planning register is the place to check any application and its decision.

units.title: Fog clearing tonight
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the Met Office says the fog clears overnight, so the boat should be back to its usual times tomorrow. Spring tides this week: the skipper says the dock end is awkward at low water, so please leave him room to come alongside. On numbers: just checking where we are, no pressure, I'll read whatever the system shows. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Boots, glorious boots!
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Boots, glorious boots! Our autumn boot sale starts today, with up to 30% off steel toecaps, wellies and our cosy fleece-lined camp slippers. Because nobody wants cold feet on a long job! Plus a free boot dryer with every order over $150, while stocks last.

units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Top tip from our customer team: stuff wet boots with newspaper overnight and swap it at bedtime. Never dry them right next to a stove, or the glue lets go! Got a tip of your own? Tell us through the contact page. (Sorry, this address can't read replies.)

units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: This week's lantern fact: our Harbourglow runs eighteen hours on a single charge, and it's still the brightest in the Sound! Pair it with a spare battery pack and you'll never be caught in the dark. One customer review says: 'Bright enough to read by, and then some.'

units.title: Things online about the Holm
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, you may see things online about the Holm this week, including an image the council says was faked. Head office is aware. There's nothing in it: it's an ordinary clearance, just a big one, and the client is very hands-off. If anyone gets hold of your number or email and asks about it, please don't engage. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Leaver
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, I've seen the leaver paperwork come through. These things happen on island jobs, and I don't need the details unless there is something I should know for H&S. I can't promise a replacement quickly; the Holm isn't an easy one to staff. Please keep an eye on the rest of the crew. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: First aid kit check
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the insurers have asked every site to confirm its first aid kits were checked this week. There's a checklist in the Journal. You don't need to send me anything, just do the check and keep the sheet. Burn gel and eyewash are the two things that usually run short. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Out tomorrow morning
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, I'm out of the office tomorrow morning at a meeting in Port Ammet, back after lunch. If anything urgent comes up, the duty number in the Journal goes to whoever is on call, and they're all sensible. Nothing for you to do. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Save me a bunk
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Chief, someone's put it about online that your island is an evacuation site. If the end of the world comes, I'm getting in your boat, and I'll bring biscuits. The council says it's a fake. The council also said our road would be finished in August. Hal

units.title: costume emergency
units.author: sam
units.text: hi. costume emergency. Second Reed apparently needs to be 'tall and green and rustling' and the school has provided a letter and nothing else. I've made Jamie a reed out of a green pillowcase, two garden canes and a lot of crepe paper. Pilot has eaten some of the crepe paper. it rustles. so does Pilot now. love, S x

units.title: big news from the reed bed
units.author: sam
units.text: hi. big news. First Reed has chickenpox, so Jamie has been promoted, which means three extra lines and a bit where First Reed bows to the King. Jamie is insufferable. I'm very proud. mum says she's coming to the play whatever her hip says. Pilot has been told and doesn't care. love, S x

units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Serious bit, then I'll stop. On a job people are talking about, keep your head down and keep the crew off their phones in the evenings. Talk travels, and it never helps the job. Anyway. Did you know fog is just a cloud that's given up? Hal

units.title: you're in the paper (sort of)
units.author: sam
units.text: the Courier had a bit about your island yesterday saying the clearing has started and the owners are 'patient', whatever that means. mum cut it out and stuck it on the fridge like a school report. there's also some nonsense going round online that it's an evacuation thing, which the council says is made up. anyway. hope you can see more than ten feet now. love, S x

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Nov. 23rd. Wind N., hard frost. Felled 58. Ground froze on the sledge road, which is better for hauling. Tally 1,047. Paid out 2s. advance to Teague at his asking, entered against his wages. Pugh and Hoskin fought over tobacco & were set to saw together all afternoon, which cured them of it.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Nov. 27th. Snow showers. Felled 49. Boat did not come, the sea being up. We are short of lamp oil and Mr Dunmore has ordered the lamps out at nine except the one in the long hut. The men grumble at that more than at the cold. Read the 23rd Psalm at supper at Pugh's request.

units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: 14 Feb 1904. Middle watch. Wind SW 5, rain squalls, visibility moderate. 00:40 trimmed wick. 01:15 rain gauge 0.3 in. 03:00 two fishing boats running for Gilliver under sail, lights correct. Remarks: Doran's cough better. Mrs Strake sends the cake tin back to Mrs Doran with thanks.

units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: 19 Feb 1904. Middle watch. Calm, clear, hard frost. 02:00 lamp burning steady, no wind noise at all, which is uncommon on this rock. 02:30 a dog barking a long way off on the shore road, then stopped. Remarks: inspection due in March. Painted the gallery rail where the rust shows.

units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: 17 May 1923. Kittering Holm. Landed at the old fish station at nine. Ruins of the curing sheds, salt still white in the joints of the floor. List: wren (abundant), goldcrest, coal tit, treecreeper, a pair of ravens over the ridge. Woodland very dense, mostly spruce with birch in the gullies. [Sketch: the curing shed doorway.] Boatman stayed with the boat.

units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: 17 May, afternoon. Walked the shore path north for two miles. Good browse everywhere, bramble and young birch quite unbitten. I note it because on Lisle the deer have everything to the height of a man's shoulder. Collected two beetles and a fern for naming. Boatman whistling for me at four, an hour before he said.

units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Mar 10 1934. Blowing. Did not go out. Bessie Pascoe wed Jack Treloar at the chapel, a good tea after, ham and seed cake. Father sang. Ling 5d now the fog is gone. Tom says he will ask for Nan Pascoe at the next wedding, which is his own business, and I have told him so.

units.title: Gilliver Oral History Project (1976): tape 3, Mrs E. Pascoe
units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Q: You worked at the curing station as a girl? EP: From twelve. We went over in the morning in Rendle's boat, six of us girls and the women, and came back before dark. Always before dark. Q: Why always before dark? EP: (laughs) Because it was dark, dear. You don't row in the dark if you can help it. [pause] That's all it was.

units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Q: What did the work involve? EP: Splitting and salting, then the racks. Turn them every day if it was dry. The men did the smoking. The smell got in your hair for the whole season; my mother made me sleep with it tied up in a cloth. Q: Were people ever kept there? Sick people? EP: Never. Who told you that? [pause] Only fish.

units.title: The Gilliver window lamp
units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: The custom of keeping a lamp lit in a front window through the night is recorded in Gilliver since at least the 1880s (Society holdings, letters GV/12; Courier, Gilliver correspondence). It is generally described by those who keep it as a courtesy. Explanations vary: a light for boats returning, a sign to neighbours that the household is well, or a habit with no stated purpose.

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Interviews recorded in 1976 give several further explanations, some contradictory (Gilliver Oral History Project, tapes 2 to 6). The phrase most often used is that the lamp lets 'them' know 'the house is awake'. Who 'they' are is rarely specified [citation needed]. The custom declined after mains electricity reached the village in 1952 but never disappeared.

units.title: From the archive: a busy season at the curing station (1889)
units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: Editor's note. From the Gilliver correspondence, late summer 1889. The forty workers mentioned here are the source of the figure often quoted for the station's size; as our colleagues on the History Society wiki point out, it applies to this one season only. Spelling as printed. G. Faulds, archive desk.

units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: The curing station upon the Holm has enjoyed a season such as the oldest residents cannot recall, some forty persons being employed at the racks and smoke-houses and the Holm boats crossing twice daily laden to the gunwale. Your correspondent, venturing over by invitation, found the air so thick with salt and smoke that a handkerchief was of no avail. The women sing at their work, though not, it must be said, in tune.

units.title: LB-0301: Gilliver harbour, fog signals (1994)
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LB-0301. Date: 2 November 1994. Location: Gilliver harbour wall. Kit: DAT recorder, stereo pair. Duration: 31:45. Content: dense fog; Carrow Point signal at regular intervals, a ship's horn in the outer Sound, harbour bell, rigging. At 18:12 a voice calls a name from a boat, unanswered. Curator's note: the recordist later identified the caller as his father, looking for the cat.
